leads.summary: An unlisted settings write converts a valid fallback bar into an empty bar
leads.consequence: A valid version:1 user shell.json with no bar (or null/nonobject bar) currently renders the builtin fallback, via shell.qml:75-90,116. If the displayed first-party clock widget calls updateEntryInline after a click (BarWidget.qml:44-56), it finds no matching entry in the raw layout, constructs empty left/center/right sections, appends an omarchy.clock entry to plugins[], and persists the config. The next barConfig read sees a now-valid empty bar, so the formerly visible fallback widgets vanish. Before this patch dirty stayed false and the same write did not persist. Treat fallback layout as canonical before writing a widget entry, or refuse insertion until the intended entry exists; do not turn missing bar into an empty persisted layout.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_opus_followup; Q1 in opus/followup-1.md, runtime plan-f2, restart plan-dc1; headline of finding F1

leads.summary: A string bar-layout entry yields a second, misplaced plugin entry instead of a settings update
leads.consequence: BarWidget/PluginRegistry normalize an entry such as bar.layout.left: ["acme.widget"] to the widget ID; updateEntryInline only compares arr[i].id, missing this valid string form. This PR's new branch now persists {id:"acme.widget",value:42} in plugins[] while leaving the visible layout string unchanged, returns true, and never delivers value:42 to that widget. Disabling the widget via PluginRegistry.setEnabled(false) removes the string layout entry but does not remove the extra plugins[] record, so a third-party widget remains enabled in the registry after it is removed from the bar. Match string entries with PluginRegistry.barEntryId()/Util.normalizeLayoutEntry() and replace the matched layout entry, rather than appending a ghost top-level record.

leads.summary: Selected replacement-bar settings are saved to plugins[] rather than bar
leads.consequence: A full-bar plugin selected by bar.id may call its exposed own-id updateEntryInline. It is not a bar.layout entry, so the new append path returns true and saves its settings under plugins[]; publicBarConfig/barConfigFor only read shellConfig.bar, so the bar sees no such change. PluginRegistry.findEntryLocation resolves bar.id before plugins[], meaning even #12260's proposed entrySettings getter reads the old bar entry, not the new record. On switching to another bar the duplicate record remains in user shell.json. Recognize selected bar-option and update config.bar (or reject with false instead of claiming success), not append another instance.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_opus_followup; Q2 in opus/followup-1.md, plan-f4; enablement and bar switching unaffected, only misfiled settings

leads.summary: New test passes with production updateEntryInline replaced by a no-op
leads.consequence: The structural checks only look for the bar handler and direct reads, not updateEntryInline. The Node section reads shell.qml into unused shellSource and then runs newly implemented JS copies of every tested production function; the fixture's canonicalWidgetId also removes the omarchy. prefix whereas the real helper preserves it. Replacing production updateEntryInline with `return false` left all eight reported assertions green under LC_ALL=C. Extract the production function into the test or run a real isolated QML fixture, and cover both bare string and object layout entries. Auto-discovery through test/shell works, but this test cannot guard the PR's added write behavior.

leads.summary: Two parallel fixes of the same QML function conflict and carry incompatible structural tests

leads.summary: The linked issue's self-write watcher premise contradicts Quickshell 0.3.1's documented FileView contract
leads.location: PR description / issue #11852, contrasted with shell/shell.qml:136-144
leads.consequence: The issue claims FileView.setText cannot trigger its own onFileChanged and therefore its own write remains stale indefinitely. Quickshell v0.3.1 fileview.hpp says watchChanges calls fileChanged when the file changes on disk, including setText/setData, and fileview.cpp installs a QFileSystemWatcher and emits on changed file/directory; the shell opts into watchChanges and reloads in that handler. The direct-read fix still addresses the synchronous read-before-later-events problem. Avoid using 'no echo ever' as a verified rationale for this PR, and if indefinite staleness matters test the exact running Quickshell/Qt combination. No GUI self-write event trace was run here.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The new `plugins[]` append in `updateEntryInline` can empty the bar.

### New `plugins[]` append can empty the bar

With no `bar` object in `shell.json` (as in the manual's idle example), right-clicking the clock saves an empty `bar.layout`, so the bar gets no widgets, even on restart. It also files settings of bare-string entries and selected bar plugins in `plugins[]`, where nothing reads them; for bare-string entries, `omarchy plugin enable`/`disable` can then break.

**Suggested change:** Drop the `!foundInPlugins` append and `break`.

<details><summary>Reproducers (fail at d1c72b6f)</summary>

Only the unit-test section of each reproducer is included here. The Quickshell runtime parts are omitted because of GitHub's comment length limit.

# Reproducer: a clock write empties the bar when shell.json has no bar object

A user `shell.json` without a `bar` object (missing, `null`, or not an object) is used as is (`applyShellConfig()` does not merge it with the defaults), so the bar comes from `builtinShellConfig.bar` (the `barConfig` binding): menu and workspaces on the left, the clock in the center, audio on the right. `updateEntryInline()` gives its working copy an empty `bar.layout` when `copy.bar` is not an object. At the base that copy is thrown away because nothing matched; at the PR head the new append marks it dirty and persists it.

## 1. Unit test in the repository's `test/shell.d` style

Save as `test/shell.d/inline-settings-no-bar-test.sh` and run it with `bash` (needs `node`). It evaluates the real `updateEntryInline` text from `shell/shell.qml` and the real `Util` helpers.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

# A user shell.json without a bar object (for example only { version, idle })
# gets the builtin fallback bar (shell.qml barConfig binding). The clock drawn
# there cycles its format with updateEntryInline("omarchy.clock", entry). That
# write must not replace the fallback with an empty bar layout.
run_node_test <<'JS'
const fs = require('fs')

function extract(file, signature) {
  const source = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, file), 'utf8')
  const start = source.indexOf(`\n  function ${signature} {`)
  if (start === -1) fail(`${file} defines ${signature}`)
  const end = source.indexOf('\n  }\n', start)
  return source.slice(start, end + 4)
}

const Util = new Function(
  extract('shell/Commons/Util.qml', 'isPlainObject(value)') +
  extract('shell/Commons/Util.qml', 'canonicalWidgetId(id)') +
  '\nreturn { isPlainObject, canonicalWidgetId }'
)()

for (const bar of [undefined, null, 'top']) {
  const shellConfig = { version: 1, idle: { screensaver: 150, lock: 300 } }
  if (bar !== undefined) shellConfig.bar = bar
  let persisted = null
  const updateEntryInline = new Function(
    'Util', 'shellConfig', 'builtinShellConfig', 'persistShellConfig',
    extract('shell/shell.qml', 'updateEntryInline(moduleName, settings)') + '\nreturn updateEntryInline'
  )(Util, shellConfig, {}, next => { persisted = next })

  const changed = updateEntryInline('omarchy.clock', { id: 'omarchy.clock', format: 'HH:mm' })
  console.log(`# bar=${JSON.stringify(bar)}: returned ${changed}; persisted ${JSON.stringify(persisted)}`)
  assert(
    persisted === null || !Util.isPlainObject(persisted.bar),
    `a clock write with bar=${JSON.stringify(bar)} does not persist a bar object (which would replace the builtin fallback bar)`
  )
}
JS
```

# Reproducer: settings for a bare-string bar entry are appended to `plugins[]`

A bar layout entry can be a bare id string (`"right": ["omarchy.power"]`); `PluginRegistry.barEntryId()`, `BarModel.entryId()` and several shell.json migrations accept that shape. `updateEntryInline()` only matches object entries (`arr[i].id`), so at the PR head such a write falls through to the new append branch.

## 1. Unit test in the repository's `test/shell.d` style

Save as `test/shell.d/inline-settings-bare-entry-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/inline-settings-bare-entry-test.sh` (needs `node`). It evaluates the real `updateEntryInline` text from `shell/shell.qml` and the real `Util` helpers from `shell/Commons/Util.qml`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

# A bar widget's layout entry may be a bare id string ("omarchy.power"); the
# registry, BarModel.entryId() and the shell.json migrations all accept that
# shape. Writing that widget's inline settings must not create a plugins[]
# entry: plugins[] is what marks a third-party plugin as enabled, and
# setEnabled() skips re-adding a widget to the bar while an entry exists.
run_node_test <<'JS'
const fs = require('fs')

function extract(file, signature) {
  const source = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, file), 'utf8')
  const start = source.indexOf(`\n  function ${signature} {`)
  if (start === -1) fail(`${file} defines ${signature}`)
  const end = source.indexOf('\n  }\n', start)
  return source.slice(start, end + 4)
}

const Util = new Function(
  extract('shell/Commons/Util.qml', 'isPlainObject(value)') +
  extract('shell/Commons/Util.qml', 'canonicalWidgetId(id)') +
  '\nreturn { isPlainObject, canonicalWidgetId }'
)()

const shellConfig = {
  version: 1,
  bar: { layout: { left: [], center: [], right: ['omarchy.power'] } },
  plugins: []
}
let persisted = null
const updateEntryInline = new Function(
  'Util', 'shellConfig', 'builtinShellConfig', 'persistShellConfig',
  extract('shell/shell.qml', 'updateEntryInline(moduleName, settings)') + '\nreturn updateEntryInline'
)(Util, shellConfig, shellConfig, next => { persisted = next })

const changed = updateEntryInline('omarchy.power', { showPercentage: true })
console.log(`# returned ${changed}; persisted plugins: ${JSON.stringify(persisted ? persisted.plugins : null)}`)
assertDeepEqual(
  persisted ? persisted.plugins : [],
  [],
  'a setting for a widget listed on the bar as a bare id is not written to plugins[]'
)
JS
```

# Reproducer: a full-bar plugin's own settings land in `plugins[]`, where the bar never sees them

A third-party bar plugin (manifest kind `bar`) selected through `bar.id` gets its shell facade from `configureBar()` (`target.shell = shell.pluginShellFor(manifest)`, `target.barConfig = shell.barConfigFor(manifest)`). Its `updateEntryInline(ownId, settings)` passes `pluginOwnsTarget` and reaches `shell.updateEntryInline(ownId, settings)`. The bar option is in neither the layout nor `plugins[]`, so at the base the call returns false; at the PR head the append adds `{ id: ownId, ...settings }` to `plugins[]`.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Runtime:** checked under Quickshell 0.3.1 and Qt 6.11.2. The config and plugin-API part of `shell/shell.qml` ran verbatim, on the offscreen platform.
- **Empty bar:** `bar` missing, `null` or `"top"` all gave the same result. At the head, `shell.json` became `"bar":{"layout":{"left":[],"center":[],"right":[]}}` plus `"plugins":[{"id":"omarchy.clock",...}]`. At the base, the write returned `false` and nothing was saved. `clock/Panel.qml` documents that as a deliberate session-only fallback.
- **Stuck widgets:** at the head, once a widget listed as a bare string (`"omarchy.power"`) has saved a setting, `setEnabled(id, false)` then `setEnabled(id, true, {})` does not put it back: the leftover `plugins[]` entry makes `setEnabled` skip re-adding it. A third-party widget with a bare-string entry that saved its own setting stays enabled after disabling, and its service stays loaded.
- **Bar-plugin settings:** a bar plugin selected through `bar.id` gets `true` back for its own write, but never receives the saved settings.
- **Where the change goes:** the unit tests above pass at the base, on current `quattro`, and at the head with only the append removed.
</details>

### Writes from `barConfig` handlers are lost

In `persistShellConfig()`, plugins now see the new value before `setText(...)` runs. A save from that notification is overwritten on disk by the older payload (3/3 runs at head, 0/3 at base).

**Suggested change:** Call `userConfigFile.setText(...)` before assigning `shellConfig`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at d1c72b6f)</summary>

# Reproducer: a plugin's write from its `barConfig` change handler is lost

With the PR, plugins receive the new `barConfig` while `persistShellConfig()` is still running: after `shellConfig = payload` and before `userConfigFile.setText(...)`. A plugin that writes a setting from that notification gets its nested write saved first, then the outer call writes its older payload over it.

The plugin below acts once on each new `mode` it sees and records `derivedFrom: <mode>` with `updateEntryInline()`. The harness changes `mode` from A to B through `PluginRegistry.setBarWidget()`, the call behind `omarchy bar set`, waits 1.5 s and reads `shell.json` from disk.

Runs the config, bar-config and plugin-API part of the real `shell/shell.qml` (kept verbatim; the bar loaders and everything from the on-demand panels section on are removed) with the real `shell/services` and `shell/Commons`, under Quickshell on the offscreen platform (no compositor needed). Tested with Quickshell 0.3.1 and Qt 6.11.2. Put these files in one directory and run `bash run.sh head /path/to/omarchy-checkout`.

`run.sh`

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: run.sh LABEL OMARCHY_CHECKOUT
# Builds a window-less copy of shell/shell.qml (config, bar-config and plugin
# API code kept verbatim; bar loaders and everything from the on-demand panels
# section on removed), installs one third-party service plugin, runs it under
# Quickshell on the offscreen platform and prints what reached shell.json.
set -u
ulimit -c 0
label=$1 src=$2
here=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
work=$(mktemp -d)
cfg="$work/cfg" home="$work/home" rt="$work/rt"
mkdir -p "$home/.config/omarchy/plugins" "$home/.cache" "$home/.local/state" "$rt" "$work/omarchy"
chmod 700 "$rt"
python3 "$here/build_harness.py" "$src" "$cfg" "$here/append.qml" "$work/build.json" || exit 2
cp -r "$here/plugins/test.sync" "$home/.config/omarchy/plugins/"
cp "$here/shell.json" "$home/.config/omarchy/shell.json"
env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME="$home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$home/.config" \
  XDG_CACHE_HOME="$home/.cache" XDG_STATE_HOME="$home/.local/state" \
  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$rt" QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OMARCHY_PATH="$work/omarchy" \
  HARNESS_OUT="$work/result.json" \
  timeout 40 quickshell -p "$cfg" --no-color >"$work/quickshell.log" 2>&1
```

`build_harness.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a window-less Quickshell harness from a source tree's shell/shell.qml.

The config/bar-config/plugin-API part of shell.qml (everything before the
"on-demand panels" section) is kept byte-for-byte, except:
  - the `import "plugins/bar"` line (the bar is not loaded),
  - the default-bar Component and the two bar Loaders (need a Wayland bar),
  - quattro's BrightnessKeys property (unrelated; needs Hyprland),
and the file is truncated at the on-demand panels marker, where the harness
code is appended. services/ and Commons/ are copied unchanged.
"""
import hashlib, json, shutil, sys
from pathlib import Path

src, cfg, append_path, report_path = map(Path, sys.argv[1:5])
text = (src / "shell/shell.qml").read_text()
report = {"source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest(), "removed": []}

def cut(t, start, end, label):
    i = t.find(start)
    assert i != -1 and t.find(start, i + 1) == -1, f"{label}: start marker not unique"
    j = t.find(end, i)
    assert j != -1, f"{label}: end marker missing"
    report["removed"].append({"label": label, "text": t[i:j]})
    return t[:i] + t[j:]

line = 'import "plugins/bar"\n'
assert text.count(line) == 1
report["removed"].append({"label": "bar import", "text": line})
text = text.replace(line, "")

bk = "  property BrightnessKeys brightnessKeys: BrightnessKeys { host: shell }\n"
if bk in text:
    report["removed"].append({"label": "BrightnessKeys", "text": bk})
    text = text.replace(bk, "")

text = cut(text, "  Component {\n    id: defaultBarComponent\n",
           "  // ------------------------------------------------------------- services",
           "default bar component and loaders")

marker = "  // ---------------------------------------------------------- on-demand panels"
assert text.count(marker) == 1, "panels marker"
k = text.find(marker)
report["removed"].append({"label": "truncated tail (panels, widgets, IPC)", "chars": len(text) - k})
text = text[:k] + Path(append_path).read_text() + "}\n"

cfg.mkdir(parents=True)
(cfg / "shell.qml").write_text(text)
shutil.copytree(src / "shell/services", cfg / "services")
shutil.copytree(src / "shell/Commons", cfg / "Commons")
report["harness_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()
Path(report_path).write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
```

```qml
import QtQuick

// A third-party service that acts once on each new "mode" it sees in
// shell.barConfig and records what it handled next to it, with
// shell.updateEntryInline().
QtObject {
  id: svc

  property var shell: null
  property var manifest: null
  property var seen: []
  property string handled: "A"

  function entry() {
    var layout = svc.shell && svc.shell.barConfig ? svc.shell.barConfig.layout : null
    var center = layout && layout.center ? layout.center : []
    for (var i = 0; i < center.length; i++)
      if (center[i] && center[i].id === "test.sync") return center[i]
    return null
  }

  property Connections watch: Connections {
    target: svc.shell
    function onBarConfigChanged() {
      var e = svc.entry()
      if (!e) return
      svc.seen.push(String(e.mode))
      if (e.mode === svc.handled) return
      svc.handled = e.mode
      svc.shell.updateEntryInline("test.sync", { mode: e.mode, derivedFrom: e.mode })
    }
  }
}
```
